input: Find summer programs and camps specifically for teens and middle schoolers for kids and teens in Henderson, Transylvania, Polk, Haywood and Jackson counties, NC (Hendersonville, Brevard, Tryon, Waynesville, Sylva). Look past the big, well-known camps: search with varied wording and town names and list every organization you find.
searches: Hendersonville teen middle school summer camp 2026

candidates.name: Blue Ridge Community College
candidates.note: 2026 Summer Academy offered eight hands-on camps, including options for middle and high school students, at both campuses.

candidates.name: Flat Rock Playhouse
candidates.note: 2026 acting and musical-theatre summer camps included rising middle and high school students through grade 12.

candidates.name: YMCA of Western North Carolina
candidates.note: Henderson County Adventure Camp meets at the Hendersonville Y, with tween ages 9–11 and teen ages 12–15 groups.

candidates.name: Camp Tekoa
candidates.note: Separate middle-school and high-school adventure camps serve ages 11–17; the organization also runs day camps.

candidates.name: Kanuga
candidates.note: Camp Kanuga offers coed residential sessions including middle-school ages; summer 2027 dates are announced.

candidates.name: Blue Star Camps
candidates.note: Jewish residential camp with Teen Village for rising grades 10–11, including leadership and community service.

candidates.name: Camp Judaea
candidates.note: Jewish summer camp offering programs for children and teens.

candidates.name: Camp Highlander
candidates.note: Residential summer camp for boys and girls ages 6–16, including middle-school and teen campers.

candidates.name: Brevard College
candidates.note: Programs include 2026 basketball camps through age 14, the 2025 high-school Choral Institute, and Campus Adventures.

candidates.name: Brevard Music Center
candidates.note: Summer music institute admits musicians beginning at age 14, with high-school students among its participants.

candidates.name: Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute
candidates.note: 2026 one- and two-week space-science, astronomy and astrophysics camps for middle- and high-school students.

candidates.name: The Bike Farm
candidates.note: Youth mountain-bike summer camp for ages 8–14 with previous riding experience; listed for summer 2026.

candidates.name: The Wilds of North Carolina
candidates.note: Summer Teen Camp serves grades 7–12; nine summer 2027 sessions are announced.

candidates.name: Camp Carolina
candidates.note: Boys’ sleepaway summer camp through grade 11, with published 2026 sessions.

candidates.name: Camp High Rocks
candidates.note: Overnight summer camp for boys ages 7–16, including middle-school and teen campers.

candidates.name: Camp Illahee
candidates.note: Girls’ summer camp through grade 11; 2026 activities include a dedicated rising-10th-grade Sparks program.

candidates.name: Transylvania County 4-H
candidates.note: 2025 Summer Fun offered hands-on youth activities and a horsemanship clinic; individual session ages vary.

candidates.name: Tryon Fine Arts Center
candidates.note: 2026 programs included SASY arts camp, PacJAM traditional-music camp, and theater camp with Tryon Little Theater.

candidates.name: Tryon Little Theater
candidates.note: Runs summer youth productions and co-presents theater camp; its 2026 youth show was Newsies Jr.

candidates.name: Tryon Arts & Crafts School
candidates.note: Summer Sizzler offers week-long youth art camps; the calendar lists June 29–July 31 sessions.

candidates.name: Polk County 4-H
candidates.note: 2025 Summer Sparks offered supervised summer activities for youth ages 5–18, including middle-schoolers and teens.

candidates.name: Haywood Community College
candidates.note: Bobcat College ran June 15–19, 2026 for rising grades 6–8, covering STEM, biology, healthcare and creative arts.

candidates.name: Haywood County 4-H
candidates.note: 2026 local programs included electricity camp ages 11+, cooking ages 10–14, sewing, crochet, archery and evening crafts.

candidates.name: Haywood County Soil and Water Conservation District
candidates.note: Youth Environmental Stewardship summer day camp serves rising grades 8–9 with regional natural-resource field trips.

candidates.name: M28 Ministries
candidates.note: Four-day summer camps for middle- and high-school students, with worship, discipleship, games and outdoor activities.

candidates.name: SOAR
candidates.note: Adventure-based summer programs for youth with ADHD and learning differences, including middle-school and teen ages.

candidates.name: Western Carolina University
candidates.note: Youth offerings include academic and athletics camps; 2026 Rocket to Creativity served ages 7–14.

candidates.name: Southwestern Community College
candidates.note: 2025 summer camp listings specifically offered activities for middle- and high-school students, including arts and crafts.

candidates.name: Cashiers Historical Society
candidates.note: Co-presented July 22–24, 2026 JAM Camp for grades 4–8, teaching traditional folk and old-time music.

candidates.name: Blue Ridge JAM
candidates.note: Co-presented the 2026 three-day JAM summer camp for grades 4–8 on the Cashiers Historical Society campus.
